title: Training-Free Generative Sampling via Moment-Matched Score Smoothing
claim: Naive smoothing of the empirical distribution distorts the data geometry as bandwidth grows; a moment-matching correction preserves it.
layout: 2 rows by 4 columns, bandwidth increasing left to right, naive above corrected
description: A 2x4 grid of 2D density heatmaps on a pale background. Each panel shows a blue density, darker where the density is higher, over 12 red triangles that mark training samples on a dashed grey unit circle. The top row is titled 'Naive density (10)'. The bottom row is titled 'Moment-matched density (20)'. Bandwidth increases from left to right. At small bandwidth, both rows show 12 separate blobs, one at each triangle. At moderate bandwidth, the naive density becomes a ring that shrinks inward. At the largest bandwidth, the naive density collapses into a single blob at the centre, away from the circle. The moment-matched row stays a clean ring on the circle at every bandwidth and only gets slightly wider. The eye goes first to the collapsed centre blob in the top right, then to the intact ring below it.
caption: Naive (top) and moment-matched (bottom) densities under isotropic Gaussian smoothing on a 2D circle, with increasing bandwidth $\sigma$ (left to right: $\sigma=0.05, 0.20, 0.45, 0.65$). Red triangles denote training samples; the dashed curve indicates the underlying unit circle. The moment-matched correction restores the circular geometry across all bandwidths.
abstract: Diffusion models generate samples by denoising along the score of a perturbed target distribution. In practice, one trains a neural diffusion model, which is computationally expensive. Recent work suggests that score matching implicitly smooths the empirical score, and that this smoothing bias promotes generalization by capturing low-dimensional data geometry. We propose moment-matched score-smoothed overdamped Langevin dynamics (MM-SOLD), a training-free interacting particle sampler that enforces the target moments throughout the sampling trajectory. We prove that the one-particle marginal of the ideal constrained Gibbs equilibrium converges, as the number of particles grows, to a Gibbs--Boltzmann density obtained by exponentially tilting the naive score-smoothed target. Its mean and covariance match the training GMM, even for rank-deficient data. We additionally establish sampling consistency, statistical target-error bounds for bounded data, and consistency of a safeguarded BAOAB-based tilting estimator. Experiments on 2D distributions and latent-space image generation show that MM-SOLD enables fast, robust, latent sampling on CPUs using fixed pretrained autoencoders, with sample fidelity and diversity competitive with neural diffusion baselines.
